An ear shattering screech echoed through the forest as Sha'fu, warrior of tribe of Med'ja-Hom sworn to the Goddess Zille plunged his blade into the eye of his foe. The great spider staggered back as thick yellow ichor oozed from its eye, Sha'fu pressed his attack, defty amputating one of the creature's mandibles with a stroke of his blade. "Times had changed" Sha'fu thought.

Before the coming of the Bird-men from the north and the discovery of metal, The Med'ja-Hom had been restricted to the use of spears and arrows. This made fighting foes such as the great spiders difficult. The weight of a long spear prevented the use of a shield and the lighter throwing spears were useless against the spiders tough hide. Close combat against a foe of such size was nigh impossible, requiring a coordinated effort from multiple Med'ja warriors.

The ease with which he was dispatching his enemy surprised the old warrior, it appeared these creatures had forgotten their purpose. Some would merely lie in wait until something disturbed their web before attacking, these could be avoided while those he came across on foot would attempt to take him down with a frontal assault, completely discarding any element of surprise by releasing a loud shriek as they charged. "Had they forgotten the temple? had they forgotten why Hom had placed them upon the earth?"

Still Sha'fu was not one to complain; creatures as simple minded as these were much prefered to the creatures he faced in his homeland. large intelligent reptiles with razor sharp claws and a nasty tendency to drop down on him from the trees above; his body bared several new scars as testament to their encounters and swift agile mammals

Sha'fu had spent much time in the land of these great spiders, the sun having rise and set 5 times since he crossed their border. The forest was darker here, the air heavier, as though the webs of the great beasts had bound the air itself. The water tasted bitter, tainted by some unknown element which Zille had assured him was harmless and strange dark colored berries grew on small bushes which grew at the bases of the forests tall trees, Zille had told Sha'fu that these were known as Nightberries a cousin to the Dew Catcher which grew in the plains to the north.

Through determination and the guidance of his Goddess the old warrior pressed onwards, ever closer to his goal.

----

Three more times the sun would rise and set before Sha'fu set his eyes upon the temple grounds, the weary warrior reinvigorated by its sight. The temple was the largest building (and of course the only building) Sha'fu had ever seen with a doorway that rose to match the height of the trees themselves; Made from a strange pale white stone the Temple looked as though it had sat undisturbed since the dawn of Gaea.

The old warrior began to run towards the temple, his heart filled with joy. It wasn't until he reached the temple doors that he remembered himself and the foe he had yet to face.

The doors of the temple lay broken upon the temples tiled floor, the splintered fragments covered in a dense sticky web. Slowly and carefully Sha'fu retreated from the temple doorway, he could not cut his way through the Spider Queen's web lest he risk alerting her of his presence. Sha'fu examined the outside of the temple searching for an alternate entrance but found only the smooth, flawless stone of the temple walls. Sha'fu had one option left.

Returning to the forest Sha'fu cut the strap that held his shield to his back and affixed it to a small branch, forming a rudimentary bow. Using the bow with a collection of branches and bark foraged the forest floor Sha'fu fabricated a torch. Thanking Flox and Valdi for their gifts the old warrior returned to the temple to claim his destiny.

With a hiss the web slowly began to part and step by step Sha'fu entered deeper and deeper into the temple. The interior of the temple appeared to be a large single hallway which lead to the inner sanctum and Hom's great treasure, if there were other hallways Sha'fu could not see them for the were obscured by the spider's web.

At the end of the hallway Sha'fu encountered another large door however this one was intact. With his options limited Sha'fu decided to ignite the door with his torch and wait for an entrance to present itself. Observing the ever expanding hallway as the web and door burned Sha'fu wondered why Hom had abandoned the temple to the spider's rule when the Med'ja would have made much better guardians. Queen Mara and her kind were primitive, mindless and prone to wander, they lacked the discipline needed to guard a treasure as valuable as the Heart of Gaea. A Shadow descended from above the door and as it came into view Sha'fu cursed himself a fool for allowing his mind to wander.

Mara, Queen of the Spiders of Hom and true Guardian of the temple lowered herself to the floor, turning her large, crimson eyes upon the diminuative interloper that had entered her lair. It had been many years since someone had entered her lair and the Queen was very hungry.

Sha'fu, foolish warrior of the Med'ja-Hom dropped his torch and fled as the Spider Queen bore down upon him; though he had slain her children with ease Mara towered over him with a size five times greater than even the largest of her kin. Praying that he would outrun her but knowing that it was impossible Sha'fu found himself flung foward as he was struck by the Queen's leg, crashing to the ground.

With death moments away Sha'fu rolled onto his back, sword at the ready and drove the blade upwards striking the Queen just below the mouth, the Queen pulling back with a shriek sending the small blade skittering across the floor. Sha'fu rose and readied his shield, preparing for the beasts second onslaught, though he was without weapon he was not without a way to defend himself. Sidestepping the Queen's foot as she attempted to trample the old warrior underneath Sha'fu lashed out with a vicious shield bash, his arm going numb as he struck the Queen's trunk-like leg.

Enraged, the Queen grasped the tiny shield between her pedipalps casting it aside, unfortunately for Sha'fu he too was cast aside as his arm was still presently attached to the shield, and so he soard through the air landing with such an impact that the breath was driven from his lungs.

Sha'fu's strength was fading, his body too old to withstand such forceful blows. As the Queen bore down upon him for the last time he raised the shattered remains of his shield and made a prayer thanking the Goddess Zille for she had loved him and granted him the warriors death which, no matter how much drink he consumed, he had been too afraid to seek out.

Just as the prayer was finished and the Queen's shadow fell over her prey the tiles of the temple floor cracked open and burst upwards as large thorned vines began to fill the hallway, shielding the warrior from the Spider Queen's wrath. Mara hissed in rage as thorns dug at her body forcing her back from her prey and obstructing her path, driving her ever backwards to the now smoldering door.

Sha'fu rose slowly, his body racked with pain as the voice of the Goddess echoed in his mind "Dear Sha'fu, I hope you did not think I had abandoned you, now pick up your blade and slay this foul beast so that you may claim your destiny"

Slowly, agonizingly, Sha'fu climbed the vines the Goddess had provided until at last he spied his foe. Now beneath him the Spider Queen stood, her body as close to the vines as possible as she tried to avoid the heat of the flaming door. With the last of his strength Sha'fu threw himself upon the Queen driving his blade deep between her eyes. The Queen let out a cry far more terrible than any before and began thrashing to and fro impaling herself upon many of the vines thorns; tearing herself free Mara crashed into the temple doors before collapsing and with a shudder died.

---

Sha'fu lay upon the vine, the last of his energy expended by the fall. Slipping into unconsciousness the old warrior caught sight of a single tree within the courtyard beyond the door and smiled; golden and glowing with an inner light, several small orbs hung from the tree's branches dancing in the breeze. He had found the Heart of Gaea.

Zille is pleased by the Med'ja-Hom's dedication to her. Sna'fu, my little hero.
